title: Data Collection and Indexing Standards
purpose: Establish mandatory standards for data collection, indexing, naming, and cross-referencing across all repository resource types. The efficiency_report.json audit scored repository data management at 4/10 with 35% storage overhead, 8 duplications, 12 inconsistencies, and 6 orphaned references. This SOP defines the three-tier index system, required fields per tier, naming conventions, cross-reference format, and automated validation requirements to prevent future drift.
scope: All repository resource types: knowledge base entries (KB), scripts (SCR), SOPs (SOP), data files (DATA), sources (SRC), tools (TOOL). Applies to any operation that creates, modifies, or deletes indexed resources.

high_severity: DUP-001: unified_benchmarks.json and final_analysis.json overlap (~8KB redundant)
DUP-002: unified_benchmarks.json and empirical_benchmarks.json overlap (~6KB redundant)
medium_severity: DUP-003: Contention data duplicated across final_analysis and empirical_benchmarks
DUP-004: KB-0012 and KB-0013 identical content
DUP-005: SRC-0018 and SRC-0039 both FRED API
duplications_found.root_cause: No deduplication checks before creating entries. No cross-reference system to link related data.

critical_count_mismatches: INC-001: KB count differs across tiers (SUMMARY=33, index=32, COMPACT=31, files=33)
INC-002: SCR count differs (SUMMARY=54, index=54, COMPACT=50, local SUMMARY=50)
INC-003: SOP count differs (SUMMARY=23, index=20, COMPACT=18)
schema_inconsistencies: INC-005: 5 different date field names across data files
INC-006: Different entry schemas per subsystem index
INC-007: Different count field names per subsystem
inconsistencies_found.root_cause: No automated synchronization between index tiers. No shared schema definition.

examples: ORP-001: KB-0033.md exists on disk, not in any index
ORP-003: SCR-0051 through SCR-0054 in index.json but missing from INDEX_COMPACT
ORP-006: 12+ script files on disk with no index entry
orphaned_references.root_cause: No validation step after creating files. No check that all tiers are updated together.

schema_issues.no_shared_schema: SCH-001: KB, SCR, SOP, DATA each have different entry schemas with no common base fields
schema_issues.duplicate_ids: SCH-002: SOP-012 and SOP-016 have duplicate IDs (v1 and v2 share same ID)
schema_issues.no_tier_spec: SCH-003: Three-tier index system has no formal specification for which fields each tier must include
schema_issues.inconsistent_crossrefs: SCH-004: Cross-references use 3 different formats (ID arrays, path strings, dot-notation)

three_tier_index_system.description: Every resource subsystem MUST maintain exactly three index tiers, generated from a single source of truth (index.json). INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json are derived views.

tier_1_summary.purpose: Quick counts and metadata for lightweight agent lookups. Minimal token cost.

required_fields.resource_type: KB | SCR | SOP | DATA | SRC | TOOL
required_fields.categories: Object mapping category names to counts
required_fields.last_modified_entry: ID of most recently modified entry

tier_2_compact.purpose: Searchable listing with key fields for each entry. Agents use this for discovery without reading full entries.

required_fields_per_entry.title: Human-readable title
required_fields_per_entry.date: ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD). Use 'date' field name universally.
required_fields_per_entry.category: Category string (never null). Must be one of the defined categories for the resource type.

tier_3_full.purpose: Complete index with all metadata. Source of truth for generating other tiers.

required_fields_per_entry.id: Unique identifier. MUST be globally unique across all resource types.
required_fields_per_entry.title: Human-readable title
required_fields_per_entry.filename: Path to the actual file, relative to the subsystem root. Use consistent convention (no mixed ../ paths).

tier_3_full.update_trigger: Any entry creation, modification, or deletion

id_format.rule: IDs are assigned sequentially and NEVER reused. Superseded entries keep their ID with a version suffix (e.g., SOP-012 v2 supersedes SOP-012 v1). Use distinct IDs in index to avoid SCH-002 collisions.

filename_format.scripts: snake_case.py or kebab-case.py (pick ONE per subsystem and stick with it). Recommendation: snake_case for Python files.
filename_format.rule: No mixed conventions within a subsystem. See INC-011: scripts currently mix hyphens and underscores. New scripts MUST use snake_case.

path_format.rule: All paths in index entries MUST be relative to the subsystem root directory. Never use ../ paths (see INC-012). Never use absolute paths.

tag_format.rule: All tags MUST be lowercase. No duplicate tags with different casing (see DUP-007: 'sops' vs 'SOPs').
tag_format.normalization: Before adding a tag, lowercase it and check for existing exact match in tag_index.

date_format.rule: Use 'date' as the field name universally. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. This resolves INC-005 (5 different date field names).

standard_format.type: KB | SCR | SOP | DATA | SRC | TOOL
standard_format.id: The target resource ID (e.g., KB-0032, SCR-0051)
standard_format.path: Optional. JSON dot-notation path to specific section within the target (e.g., 'contention_analysis.results')

cross_reference_format.rule: All cross-references MUST use this format. Deprecated formats (bare ID arrays, path strings, dot-notation without type) must be migrated. See SCH-004.
cross_reference_format.validation: The referenced ID must exist in the target subsystem's index.json. Orphaned cross-references must be flagged by automated validation.

procedures.title: Check for Duplicates Before Creating
procedures.action: Before creating any new entry, search INDEX_COMPACT.json for the relevant resource type. Check for entries with similar titles, overlapping content, or identical data sources. If a potential duplicate is found, extend the existing entry instead of creating a new one.
duplicate_check_method: Check tag_index for entries with the same tags
For data files: check if the same data source or benchmark run already has an entry
For KB entries: check builds_on chains for related prior work
procedures.output: Duplicate check result: 'no duplicate found' or 'potential duplicate: <ID>, recommend extending'

procedures.title: Assign ID and Create Entry
procedures.action: Assign the next sequential ID for the resource type. Create the entry file following naming conventions.
procedures.id_assignment: Read the current highest ID from index.json. Increment by 1. Never reuse deleted or superseded IDs.
procedures.output: New entry file created with correct ID and filename

procedures.title: Update All Three Index Tiers
procedures.action: Update index.json, INDEX_COMPACT.json, and SUMMARY.json for the relevant subsystem. All three MUST be updated in the same operation.
update_order: 1. Add entry to index.json (source of truth) with all required fields
2. Add entry to INDEX_COMPACT.json with required compact fields
4. If a global INDEX_COMPACT.json or SUMMARY.json exists in storage/data/, update those too
procedures.critical_rule: NEVER update only one tier. If you update index.json, you MUST also update INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json in the same commit. This prevents the drift that caused INC-001 through INC-003.
procedures.output: All three tiers updated and consistent

procedures.title: Add Cross-References
procedures.action: For any new entry that references other resources, add cross-references using the standard format. Verify that all referenced IDs exist in their respective indexes.
validation: Each cross-reference target ID must exist in the target subsystem's index.json
Each cross-reference path (if specified) must be a valid JSON path in the target file
Bidirectional references are encouraged: if A references B, B should reference A

procedures.title: Run Automated Validation
procedures.action: After any index modification, run the validation checks to ensure consistency across all tiers.
validation_checks: Count consistency: entry_count in SUMMARY matches array length in INDEX_COMPACT matches array length in index.json
Coverage: every file on disk in the subsystem directory has a corresponding index entry
No orphans: every index entry points to a file that exists on disk
No duplicate IDs: every ID in index.json is unique
Schema compliance: every entry has all required fields for its resource type
Cross-reference validity: every referenced ID exists in the target index
Tag normalization: all tags are lowercase with no duplicates
procedures.tools: Use auto_index.py, cross_ref_checker.py, validate_naming.py, kb_validator.py as applicable

actions: 1. Duplicate check against INDEX_COMPACT.json
2. Assign next sequential ID
3. Create entry file with correct naming convention
4. Update index.json with all required + type-specific fields
5. Update INDEX_COMPACT.json with required compact fields
6. Update SUMMARY.json (increment entry_count, update categories)
7. Update global storage/data/ indexes if they exist
8. Add cross-references in standard format
9. Run validation checks
1. Update the entry file
2. Update index.json if any indexed fields changed (title, category, status, tags)
3. Update INDEX_COMPACT.json if compact fields changed
4. Update SUMMARY.json if category or status changed (affects counts)
5. Verify cross-references still valid
6. Run validation checks
1. Set status to 'deprecated' in index.json (prefer deprecation over deletion)
2. Update INDEX_COMPACT.json status field
3. Update SUMMARY.json (decrement active entry_count if removing from active set)
4. Check for incoming cross-references from other entries and update them
5. Run validation checks
step_2c.rule: Never delete an ID from the index. Mark as deprecated. This preserves cross-reference integrity.

actions: 1. Perform all individual entry operations first
2. Run auto_index.py to regenerate INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json from index.json
3. Run full validation suite
4. Verify all counts match across tiers
step_2d.rationale: For bulk operations, regenerating derived tiers from source of truth is more reliable than incremental updates.

anti_patterns.name: Update One Tier Only
anti_patterns.description: Adding an entry to index.json but forgetting to update INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: This is the root cause of INC-001 through INC-003 and ORP-002 through ORP-004 in the efficiency report. Agents querying INDEX_COMPACT miss entries that exist in the full index. Count mismatches confuse tooling.
anti_patterns.fix: ALWAYS update all three tiers in the same operation. Use auto_index.py for regeneration when possible.

anti_patterns.name: File Without Index Entry
anti_patterns.description: Creating a file on disk without registering it in any index.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: ORP-006 found 12+ unregistered script files on disk. These files are invisible to any index-based lookup, making them effectively undiscoverable.
anti_patterns.fix: Every file in an indexed directory MUST have a corresponding index entry. Register before or during file creation, never after.

anti_patterns.name: Inconsistent Date Fields
anti_patterns.description: Using different field names for dates across files (collected_at, run_date, analysis_date, added, generated).
anti_patterns.why_wrong: INC-005 found 5 different date field names. This makes cross-subsystem queries impossible without custom parsing logic per type.
anti_patterns.fix: Use 'date' as the universal field name. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

anti_patterns.name: Null Categories
anti_patterns.description: Setting category to null in index entries.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: INC-009 and INC-010 found all SOP and SRC entries have null categories. This defeats category-based filtering and aggregation.
anti_patterns.fix: Every entry MUST have a non-null category. Define a category taxonomy per resource type and enforce it.

anti_patterns.name: Mixed Cross-Reference Formats
anti_patterns.description: Using bare ID arrays in one file, path strings in another, and dot-notation in a third.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: SCH-004 found 3 different cross-reference formats. Tooling cannot follow references without format-specific parsers.

anti_patterns.name: Duplicate IDs for Versioned Entries
anti_patterns.description: Using the same ID for both v1 and v2 of a superseded entry.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: SCH-002 found SOP-012 and SOP-016 have duplicate IDs. This breaks ID uniqueness and confuses cross-references.
anti_patterns.fix: Superseded entries keep their original ID with status 'superseded'. New versions get new IDs, or use version suffix (SOP-012-v2).

references.data_points: 4/10 score, 35% overhead, 8 duplications, 12 inconsistencies, 6 orphaned references
8 duplication instances with severity and recommendations
12 inconsistency instances across count mismatches, schema issues, and naming
6 orphaned reference instances including 12+ unregistered files
4 schema issues: no shared schema, duplicate IDs, no tier spec, inconsistent crossrefs
10 prioritized recommendations for fixing data management issues
Token efficiency: 90.2% reduction enables 11.7x more I/O per context window, making index reads cheap

compliance_indicators: All three index tiers updated together for every entry change
Zero count mismatches between SUMMARY, INDEX_COMPACT, and index.json
Zero orphaned files (files on disk without index entries)
Zero orphaned index entries (entries pointing to nonexistent files)
Zero null categories in any index entry
All cross-references use standard format and point to valid targets
All tags normalized to lowercase with no duplicates
All date fields use 'date' as the field name with YYYY-MM-DD format
Validation checks run after every index modification
metrics.measurement_method: Run efficiency_report.json-equivalent audit monthly. Track score, overhead, and issue counts over time. Flag any regression from previous audit.
